title: Kernel sequencer + staged warmup for FlashAttention v2/v3 compatibility
creator: Aisha Raman
body:
Summary:
We are seeing intermittent tail-latency regressions when switching between FlashAttention v2 and FlashAttention v3 kernels during cold startup and prefill phases for mixed sequence-length traffic. This ticket proposes a lightweight 'kernel sequencer' and a staged warmup for prefill/first-decode that smooths transitions between kernel families and reduces workspace allocation churn. The goal is to reduce 99th/99.9th percentile latency spikes without sacrificing throughput or regressing token-cost economics.

Problem statement and evidence:
- Incidents: multiple customer reports and internal perf runs show transient latency spikes (~2.5-3x P99) for workloads with bursts of short (<64) then long (>1024) sequences.
- Repro: perf harness runs (2025-02-12) on A100-40G demonstrated workspace thrash: kernel fallback to FA2 when FA3 workspace allocation fails, causing repeated allocation/free cycles and decoder stalls.
- Related tickets: ENG-118901 (startup shims), ENG-100213 (workspace reuse), ENG-84211 (quantized routing) provide context and partial fixes but do not address sequencing logic.

Hypothesis:
- A simple sequencer that selects an ordered list of candidate kernels per request class (seq_len profile, quantization, batch size) and performs an inexpensive staged warmup (probe + lightweight priming invocation) will reduce unnecessary kernel swaps and workspace churn during prefill and first decode windows.

Design overview:
- Kernel sequencer component: per-model policy that ranks kernels (FA3, FA2, naive) with heuristics based on seq_len, cached-KV footprint estimate, and recent success rate.
- Staged warmup: when a new kernel pair is chosen, the runtime will run up to N small priming invocations (configurable; default N=2) that avoid full decoding but allocate/validate workspace and KV cache shapes.
- Probe backoff: if priming fails due to workspace constraints, sequencer falls back but increases backoff timeout to avoid flip-flopping for the same model instance.
- Metrics and telemetry: record kernel_choice, priming_result, allocation_failure_reason, and per-request kernel_switch_count. Expose rollup charts for P50/P95/P99 latency pre/post warmup per model.

Acceptance criteria:
- Measured P99 latency reduction >= 30% in synthetic mixed-length workload (replicate customer pattern) compared to control (no sequencer).
- No CPU or GPU memory leak across 24h soak test.
- No throughput regression > 5% at target QPS for dedicated capacity profiles.
- Automated canary rollout steps documented and reversible.

Test plan:
- Local perf harness: run mixed-length trace (short bursts then long sequences) with 500k tokens warmup. Compare control vs sequencer variants (N=0,1,2,4).
- Dedicated cluster canary: route 1% traffic to sequencer on runtime-1.22 canary pool; monitor P99, kernel_switch_count, allocation_failures for 6 hours.
- E2E customer replay: sample production trace from customer X (sanitized) and run against runtime image with sequencer enabled.

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag gated: runtime flag kernel_sequencer={off,gradual,aggressive}. Default off.
- Canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 72h with observability checks at each step and automatic rollback on P99 > baseline * 1.5.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: priming adds small CPU/GPU overhead early. Mitigation: probe is limited to tiny allocations and bounded count; measure overhead and tune defaults.
- Risk: sequencer policy mis-ranks kernels, causing suboptimal choice. Mitigation: include fallback counter and telemetry; ability to pin per-model kernel in console and disable sequencer.

Implementation notes and files to change:
- runtime/attn/sequencer.rs: new sequencer component and policy interface.
- runtime/attn/priming.rs: staged warmup hooks and allocation validator.
- integrations/metrics: add kernel_choice, priming_result, allocation_failure_reason metrics.
- config: model-level annotation kernel_sequence_policy and global flags.

Open questions:
- Should priming use real tokens or synthetic zero-length payloads? (prefers synthetic to avoid customer data).
- Default N value for priming (experiment with 1-3).
- Backoff heuristic tuning: fixed exponential vs. adaptive based on failure reason.

Notes on compatibility with FA2/FA3:
- Sequencer must operate at the kernel ABI level and avoid introducing additional workspace layout incompatibilities. Collaboration with kernel maintainers required to enumerate safe priming shapes for each kernel family.

Documentation and dashboarding:
- Confluence: /spaces/INF/pages/Kernel+Sequencer+Design (draft).
- Dashboard: Performance -> Kernel Sequencer (new) with breakdown by model, region, and runtime.

Next steps:
- Prototype in local harness (Luca) -> bench variant runs -> submit RFC + PRs for sequencer and priming hooks.
- Coordinate with kernel owners (cc: Marion Zhao, Kenji Sato) for priming shape catalog.
comments: 2025-02-18 - triage: created by Aisha after customer-reported spikes on 2025-02-12. Assigned to Luca for prototype. Linked ENG-118901 and ENG-100213.
2025-02-20 - Luca: initial design reviewed with runtime team; scoped to 8 points. Decided to gate behind feature flag and limit priming to 2 probes by default.

2025-02-24 - Experiment: local harness (A100-40G) run with mixed-length trace. Early results: N=2 reduced observed P99 from 380ms -> 260ms (31% improvement) but increased P50 by ~4ms. Full data in perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood.dev/d/rt/kernel-sequencer-experiments
2025-02-26 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 - add sequencer interface and priming hooks. Requesting review from @marionzhao and @kensato.

2025-02-27 - Review feedback (Marion): ensure priming avoids non-deterministic kernel codepaths; prefer synthetic priming workload. Kenji: verify FA3 priming shapes will not trigger rare boundary checks.

2025-03-01 - Blocker found: cluster canary run failed in one region due to workspace accounting mismatch when quantized kernels are present. Added dependency ENG-84211 to investigate interaction. Reduced canary to 0.5% traffic and paused further rollout.
2025-03-02 - Next: Luca will add quantized-path guards to sequencer and run extended soak test 24h across GPU types (A100, H100). Target to unblock canary on 2025-03-05.
